title: Contractible full inverse-image curves and exact generic-pencil boundary defect

retained_external_foundations.statement: Characteristic-zero Riemann-Hurwitz, explicitly retained from Stacks0C1B; standard extension of a curve morphism to finite smooth projective completions. Finite-image punctures are accounted for, not silently removed.
Field-agnostic noncomposite-polynomial argument gives geometrically integral generic fibres, from retained Arzhantsev-Petravchuk Theorem1 and the reproduced denominator/disjointness argument.

retained_structural_inputs.statement: Actual rank-one closed embedding makes K a closed immersion on its radical zero curve.
A target-descended trace square gives f=a(K) and an isomorphism of the entire reduced source and target zero curves; components have affine normalization A1 under hypothetical failure.
Target irreducibles have square-free source pullbacks; birational Keller inverse denominators are removable.

cross_checked_primary_statement.role: Consistent statement of Lin-Zaidenberg, already retained; no theorem about the entire nonproperness set is newly imported.

direct_proof_arguments: The exact projective Riemann-Hurwitz decomposition gives nu_s=d nu_t+E, where E sums indices at source punctures mapping to finite target points.
One source puncture and one target puncture force E=0 by surjectivity of the nonconstant projective extension.
Separate imported contractible plane rectifications and the invariant cusp valuation semigroup identify the monomial exponents without extending an arbitrary curve isomorphism.
The full inverse image and square-free Keller pullback give one polynomial pencil identity with multiplicity one.
The monomial generic curve has a degree-p cover with q simple finite totally ramified points and one point at infinity; its genus follows directly from Riemann-Hurwitz.
The equal-genus single-puncture certificate forces Keller degree one in every coprime cusp degree.
The actual full radical-curve isomorphism applies componentwise; every descended unibranch component closes.
An A1-normalized curve with no internal multibranch point is properly bijectively normalized and is topologically A1, so hypothetical failure forces chi<=0 on every component.

Remaining source and target irreducible pencils satisfy the exact log-Euler defect identity; HW0 excludes field degree two, so a positive target invariant requires at least tripling under hypothetical failure.
